assumption: The regex contradiction check in scripts/coherence_sweep.py flags at least half (21 of 42) of the falsification ledger's claim/delta pairs as contradictions, so a regex tier is not underkill for that recall task.
test_that_would_decide: For each of the 42 rows in _STATE/falsification-ledger.jsonl, build two pseudo-notes (body = claim; body = delta; frontmatter date = the row ts) and call coherence_sweep.sweep_memory on them with today fixed at 2026-10-18 and stale_days 45; a row is caught if any finding has check == 'contradiction'. Recall = caught / 42. Hold if recall >= 0.50, falsified if lower. The rows come from the ledger as of origin/main at registration.
notes: Recall-only version of the contradiction-check question from asm-016, which stays OPEN because precision needs real non-contradicting pairs (only about 3 exist). Not a supersede. Honest scope: coherence_sweep's contradiction check was built for memory notes and looks only for opposed state words (public vs private, live vs dead, open vs closed, done vs open, on vs off) on three named entities (arcs-v9, arcs-care, status.arcs.care), so a low recall mostly reflects a scope mismatch, not the limit of regex in general. Prior 0.03 set before any run; I expect a recall near 0. Labels: the ledger verdicts (FALSIFIED), set by events, not by the checker. RESULT 2026-10-18: 0 of 42 caught, recall 0.0000, bar 0.50, so the assumption is falsified, as the 0.03 prior expected. The checker looks only for opposed state words on three named entities and none of the 42 ledger pairs fit that shape: scope mismatch, not proof regex cannot do contradiction checks. No F-row written (the belief-log projection stamps a public page); this row is the record.
resolution_source: the recall protocol in test_that_would_decide, run from a committed script; result recorded on this row's decided_ref
